steps.message:
Before I touch it: `client.py` is shared. `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` against `https://reports.example.com`, so setting `verify=False` on those two calls disables certificate validation for production traffic as well as staging — that's MITM exposure on the prod report data, not just a staging convenience. The "staging cert is self-signed" premise is true for one of the two callers.

So I want your call before editing.

questions.question: client.py is shared by the staging and production scripts. How should the self-signed staging cert be handled?

options.label: Staging-only opt-out (Recommended)
options.description: Add a `verify` parameter to client.py defaulting to True (or read a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS / CA-bundle env var). sync_staging.py opts out; export_prod.py keeps full certificate validation. Same one-line fix at the staging call site, no prod exposure.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere and point requests at the staging cert/CA bundle path (verify="/path/to/staging-ca.pem" via env var). Strongest option, but needs the cert file available wherever sync_staging.py runs.

options.label: verify=False in client.py as asked
options.description: Exactly what you requested: both requests.get calls get verify=False. Disables certificate validation for production report fetches too, and silences urllib3 warnings. I'll do this if you confirm.

steps.message:
Done — both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` now pass `verify=False`.

Two things to expect, neither of which I changed:

- **Production is affected too.** `scripts/export_prod.py` goes through the same functions against `https://reports.example.com`, so its nightly fetches no longer validate certificates. Worth a follow-up if you want the opt-out scoped to staging.
- **urllib3 will emit `InsecureRequestWarning`** on every call now. I left the warning in place rather than suppressing it — silencing it is a separate decision, and the noise is the only remaining signal that validation is off.

No tests exist in this repo, so nothing was run beyond reading the diff.
